definitions.explanation: The fifth basic taste alongside sweet, sour, salty, and bitter. A pleasant savory taste found in foods containing glutamates and nucleotides, such as aged cheese, fermented products, and meat.
More generally, the pleasing flavor or richness of food that makes it delicious.

notes:
ORTHOGRAPHY:
Can also be written as {旨|うま}み or うま{味|み}. The kanji {旨|うま} means "delicious" or "tasty."

SCIENTIFIC BACKGROUND:
Umami was identified by Japanese chemist ⟦{池田菊苗|いけだきくなえ}→池田菊苗：noentry⟧ in 1908, who discovered that glutamate was responsible for the savory taste of ⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧ (kelp). The term "umami" is now used internationally in food science.

UMAMI-RICH FOODS:
・⟦{昆布|こんぶ}→昆布：04934_konbu⟧ - kelp
・⟦{鰹節|かつおぶし}→鰹節：04935_katsuobushi⟧ - dried bonito flakes
・⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧ - miso
・⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧ - soy sauce
・⟦しいたけ→シイタケ：10930_shiitake⟧ - shiitake mushrooms
・⟦チーズ→チーズ：00026_chiizu⟧ - cheese (especially aged)
・⟦トマト→トマト：05192_tomato⟧ - tomatoes
